newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea condemns defector Hwang as "human waste".
newsitem.headline: N.Korea condemns defector Hwang as "human waste".

text.p: North Korea on Friday lashed out at a top Pyongyang defector for "slandering" the communist government and condemned him as a "human waste and lunatic".

North Korea accused Hwang Jang-yop, the highest ranking North Korean ever to flee his homeland, by quoting a statement issued by the Radio Voice of National Salvation about a news conference given by Hwang in Seoul on Thursday.
The Stalinist state says this is a pro-Pyongyang "underground" organisation in Seoul, and often uses it to launch anti-South Korea propaganda. South Korea says the organisation does not exist.
According to the official Korean News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo, the statement said:

"The behaviour of Hwang, who was tamed in a 'cage' of the ANSP (Agency for National Security Planning), at the conference proved that he was a human waste and lunatic as our people already branded him."
It was the North Korean media's first reference to the news conference by Hwang, an ideologue who helped author Pyongyang's guiding ideology of self-reliance, or "juche".
On Thursday, Hwang said North Korean leader Kim Jong-il had rejected reform in his hunger-stricken nation and was plotting a lightning war against the South as his only escape.
"Hwang had been brainwashed and trained in a secret place for more than two months since he was taken to Seoul from abroad," the statement said.
Hwang sought asylum at South Korea's Beijing consulate in February. He was then stuck for more than two months in China and the Philippines before being spirited to Seoul.
"The traitor Hwang slandered the political system of North Korea, where he had lived for scores of years," said the statement issued by the pro-Pyongyang group.
"He must be an incurable case of mental derangement as he is not able to distinguish between dictatorship and democracy," it said.
North and South Korea remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce rather than a peace treaty.
